scenes.title: Participant with EOG eye-fixation sensors locked dead-center on '+' pressing a single key 60 ms faster for the arrow-cued box
scenes.era: 1980, University of Oregon cognitive neuroscience lab, Eugene

layout.description: Clean high-key 1980 visual psychophysics lab with a chinrest facing a crisp monitor displaying a center '+' cross, a small left-pointing arrow cue above '+', and two square outline boxes on the left and right alongside an EOG flat-line eye-movement trace and millisecond counter.

positions.where: resting chin steadily on the optical chinrest with eyes locked dead-center on '+', right index finger pressing a single telegraph-style microswitch

positions.who: Michael Posner (mannequin in 1980s plaid shirt and vest)
positions.where: standing beside the EOG oscilloscope and millisecond counter comparing '235 ms Valid' against '295 ms Invalid'
positions.facing: pointing to the flat EOG eye-trace

props.name: three-element Posner screen ('[ ] +← [ ]')
props.period_detail: crisp high-contrast monitor showing central fixation cross, directional arrow cue, and peripheral target asterisk '*' flashing in the left box
props.physical_behavior: visualizes covert attention without eye movement

props.name: flat-line EOG eye-stability trace
props.period_detail: paper/oscilloscope strip confirming 0.0 degrees of physical eyeball rotation
props.physical_behavior: proves the 60 ms speedup happened purely inside the brain

props.name: dual millisecond digital readout
props.period_detail: clean 1980 LED counter contrasting ~235 ms (Valid 80%) vs ~295 ms (Invalid 20%)
props.physical_behavior: quantifies spotlight benefit plus disengagement cost

actions.verb_sequence: points LEFT while eyes stay frozen on '+' -> asterisk '*' flashes inside the left box -> Participant's finger clicks the single key in 235 ms
arrow points LEFT, asterisk flashes RIGHT -> finger hesitates to 295 ms while parietal spotlight disengages and re-aims

reactions.reaction: taps the completely flat EOG eye trace beside the 60-millisecond reaction swing

scenes.wardrobe: 1980 Pacific Northwest university wear: knit crew sweater on participant; collared plaid shirt and wool vest on researcher.
scenes.lighting: Bright clean laboratory daylight with crisp readable monitor contrast.
scenes.recognition_hook: With sensors proving their eyeballs never budged a hair from the center cross, people spot a side flash 60 milliseconds faster because an invisible mental spotlight got there first.

key_visual.description: a 1980 participant on a chinrest staring straight at a center '+' screen between two side boxes while pressing a single key beside a flat eye-movement trace and 235ms/295ms timer

scenes.title: No-look basketball pass: eyes center, spotlight on the wing

layout.description: Sunlit hardwood court where a point guard looks straight into a defender's eyes while rifling a crisp bounce pass to a cutting teammate on the left wing.

positions.where: head and eyes locked straight ahead at the defender while hands snap a precise diagonal bounce pass left
fooled by the guard's eye direction

props.name: leather basketball
props.period_detail: bouncing cleanly into the left-wing cutter's hands

actions.verb_sequence: locks eyes center -> shifts covert spotlight left -> fires pinpoint no-look pass

scenes.wardrobe: Clean white and navy athletic uniforms.
scenes.recognition_hook: Every great no-look pass exploits Posner's split between where eyes point and where attention aims.

scenes.title: Inhibition of Return after 300 milliseconds

layout.description: Close view of the two-box screen showing a brief border flash on the left followed 400 ms later by a slower response at that old flashed box.

positions.where: pointing to the crossover point at 300 ms on the timeline chart where fast pull flips into Inhibition of Return

props.name: 300-ms crossover graph
props.period_detail: clean curve dipping fast at 100 ms then rising above baseline past 300 ms

actions.verb_sequence: traces the facilitation-to-inhibition flip at 300 milliseconds

reactions.reaction: nods seeing how the spotlight refuses to get stuck on old flashes

scenes.recognition_hook: Wait a third of a second after an irrelevant flash, and your brain actively suppresses that old spot so you keep exploring.

scenes.title: Driver hanging up a heated hands-free call to return the spotlight to the road

layout.description: Bright daytime windshield view where a driver taps 'End Call' on the steering wheel so eyes AND covert spotlight reunite on merging traffic.

positions.where: pressing steering-wheel end-call button and scanning highway merge cleanly

actions.verb_sequence: ends distracting call -> spots merging cyclist immediately in peripheral lane

scenes.recognition_hook: Eyes on the windshield mean nothing if a heated phone call steals your parietal spotlight.
